title: An Integrated System to Remotely Trigger Intracellular Signal Transduction by Upconversion Nanoparticle-mediated Kinase Photoactivation
protocol: Install a 4X objective lens next to the cuvette holder of the fluorescence spectrometer.
Place a tunable 0.5- to 8-W 980-nm laser diode at a 90° angle against the objective lens.
Install a full reflectance mirror in the light path intersection of the objective lens and laser.
Place a black anodized metal plate to block the excitation window of spectroscopy.
Place the cuvette containing silica-coated UCNP solution (0.2 - 0.6 mg/mL) in the cuvette holder.
Switch the spectroscopy to luminescence mode with the lowest PMT voltage setting.
Adjust the mirror for optimal alignment, ensuring the beam is centered on the cuvette and the PMT detects the strongest signal.
Measure the upconversion spectrum after alignment with the desired power setting.
Use a thermal pile power meter to build a calibration curve of laser power against electrical current readings on the laser power supply.
Constantly check the laser performance to ensure it remains within the calibrated range.
Equip the fluorescence microscope with a metal halide light guide directed into the back port.
Ensure one cube position is empty in the upper-tier light path to allow for NIR coming from the lower-tier light path.
Install a tunable 0.5 to 8.0 W 980 nm laser diode in the right-side port.
Remove the side-port collimator to enlarge the laser light spot.
Use a dichroic mirror (850-nm short-pass) and an excitation filter (950 nm long-pass) for alignment.
Visualize the NIR light spot using a UCNP solution.
Adjust the position of the laser to center the NIR light beam in the field of view.
Incubate recombinant PKA (9 µM) with 0.5 mM 2-nitrobenzylbromide (NBB) in caging buffer for 1 - 2 h at 25 °C.
Quench excess NBB with 10 mM dithiothreitol (DTT).
Dialyze the mixture against HEPES buffer (10 mM, pH 7.5) to remove excess reagents and salts.
Mix lanthanide salts-Y(CH3CO2)3 hydrate, Yb(CH3CO2)3 hydrate, and Tm(CH3CO2)3 hydrate in octadecene and oleic acid.
Heat the mixture to 115 °C for 30 min.
Cool the mixture to 50 °C.
Dissolve the reaction mixture in a methanolic solution with NaOH pellet and ammonium fluoride by sonication for 15 min.
Increase the reaction temperature to 300 °C to obtain UCNP core (β-NaYF4:1.0% Tm3+/30% Yb3+) nanoparticles.
Dissolve core nanoparticles with CO-520 in cyclohexane.
Add ammonia and tetraethylorthosilicate to the solution.
Stir the mixture for 12 h at room temperature to get silica-coated β-NaYF4:1.0%Tm3+/30%Yb3+ core nanoparticles.
Incubate PKA or caged PKA with UCNP in HEPES buffer at 4 °C for 3 h.
Filter the mixture using PVDF filter (0.45 µm).
Centrifuge the filtered mixture at 17,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Redisperse the pellet in HEPES containing 0.1% protein stabilizer to obtain purified PKA-UCNP complex.
Centrifuge the mixture again at 17,000 x g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Collect the supernatant for a Bradford assay in a 1.5-mL tube.
Analyze the unbounded PKA in supernatant with a Bradford assay.
Back-calculate the PKA substitution level on UCNP particles using the Bradford assay results.
Determine the activity of PKA and PKA-UCNP in a 60 µL total volume of assay mixture containing MOPS, KCl, PEP, ATP, NADH, MgCl2, kemptide, and a pyruvate kinase/lactate dehydrogenase mixture.
Measure the decrease in NADH absorbance over time after adding PKA solution to the assay mixture.
Calculate the slope of the line to reflect PKA activity directly.
Measure the activity of PKA-UCNP15 and compare it with the product of native PKA-specific activity and the calculated PKA surface-coated amount.
Measure all light source powers using a thermal pile sensor.
Calculate power densities based on light spot area for 365 nm LED photolysis experiments (200 mW/cm²).
Perform UV photolysis experiments on a commercial system with a 365 nm LED.
Illuminate the PKA-UCNP solution with excitation light filtered by a commercial cube.
Measure power density estimated to be ~15 mW/cm² without objective lens focusing for UV photoactivation.
Illuminate the PKA-UCNP solution using a 980 nm laser with customized upconversion filter/mirror settings installed on the lower-tier light path.
Use a dichroic mirror (850 nm short-pass) and an excitation filter (950 nm long-pass) for in vitro NIR photoactivation.
Estimate power density to be ~68 W/cm² after 4X objective lens focusing for in vitro NIR photoactivation.
Pre-filter the samples through a 0.45 µm filter after PKA immobilization.
Incubate the cells in 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) containing L-15 medium during the microinjection period for stable pH control outside the incubator.
Co-inject native PKA-UCNP, caged PKA-UCNP, or PEGylated UCNP with TAMRA into cells.
Adjust the concentration of PKA-UCNP particles to achieve a cytosolic concentration of 1 - 3 μM after microinjection.
Perform microinjection into the cells using a microinjector device coupled with a one-axis hydraulic micromanipulator.
Monitor the pressure applied by the microinjector using a digital pressure gauge.
Seal the dispenser valve in a customized pressuring chamber to provide compensation pressure for microinjection.
Pull back the needle using a puller.
Maintain the injection pressure between 50 and 75 hPa with an injection time of 200-300 ms.
Set the compensation pressure at 15 hPa to prevent culture medium backflow into the needle by capillary action.
Examine the tip openings of the needles to ensure they have an external diameter between 1.3 and 1.5 μm.
Confirm the tip opening dimensions using images taken with a 40x objective lens.
Wash the cells with 2 mL of L-15 medium containing 10% FBS.
Observe cellular fluorescence imaging from 5(6)-carboxytetramethyl-rhodamine (TAMRA) to confirm microinjection completion.
Grow REF52 cells on a 3.5 µm dish for UV photoactivation.
Place the dish with cells on the microscope stage.
Irradiate the cells with UV light filtered by the cube without objective lens focusing for 3 min.
Illuminate the cells on a 980-nm laser from lower-tier filter/mirror settings for NIR photoactivation.
Focus the 10x objective lens during photoactivation to achieve a power density of 300 W/cm².
Irradiate the cells with NIR light focused by a 10x objective lens and collimator for 15 min when a larger light spot is needed.
Allow a 5 min dark interval after every 5-min irradiation to avoid heating.
Use the 40X objective lens with a pinhole installed in the exit end of the light guide for high spatial resolution irradiation.
Irradiate the cells for 1 s using NIR photoactivation.
Allow the cells to recover in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 1 h in complete medium after photolysis.
Fix the cells in 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde/phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) for 20 min.
Add 5 μL of 6.6 μM Alexa 594-phalloidin stock solution to 200 μL of PBS for staining.
Incubate the cells with Alexa 594-phalloidin for 25 min at room temperature.
Visualize the images of Alexa 594-phalloidin using a filter set (Ex 581 nm/Em 609 nm).
Incubate the cells for 5 min in DAPI at room temperature.
Wash the samples with PBS after staining.
Take fluorescent images of the stress fibers and nuclei separately.
